title: Term unification: substitutions and most general solutions

based_on.title: Programming Languages: A unification algorithm
based_on.pages: Transformation rules and termination argument (page dated 29 April 2004)

summary: Solve finite equations between first-order terms by substitutions, and prove that every solution is an instance of the one returned.
abstract: The expressions \(f(x,a)\) and \(f(b,y)\) become identical when \(x\) is replaced by \(b\) and \(y\) by \(a\). Finding such replacements is called unification. Some equations have no solution: replacing a variable by a finite term cannot make it equal to a function applied to itself. We give an algorithm that either detects an obstruction or returns a substitution from which every other solution can be obtained by further replacement. The proof explains both why the algorithm stops and why it preserves all possible solutions, including the freedom to choose values for variables not mentioned in the original equations.
